google: An administrator creates a Google Cloud project for your organisation.
In that project, turn on the Google Calendar API.
Set up the OAuth consent screen (internal to your Google Workspace).
Create an OAuth client of type web application, with the Pairly callback URL.
Give the client id, secret and callback URL to Pairly as PAIRLY_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, PAIRLY_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET and PAIRLY_GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URL.
Turn on the hire.scheduling.google feature flag in Settings, Feature flags.
Each interviewer then connects their own calendar here.
microsoft: An administrator registers an app in Microsoft Entra ID for your organisation (accounts in your organisational directory).
Add the delegated Microsoft Graph permissions Calendars.ReadWrite, User.Read and offline_access, and grant admin consent.
Add a web redirect URI with the Pairly callback URL and create a client secret.

Give the application id, secret and callback URL to Pairly as PAIRLY_MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID, PAIRLY_MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET and PAIRLY_MICROSOFT_REDIRECT_URL (and your tenant id as PAIRLY_MICROSOFT_TENANT, optional).
Turn on the hire.scheduling.microsoft feature flag in Settings, Feature flags.
Each interviewer then connects their own calendar here.
zoom: An administrator of your Zoom account creates a Server-to-Server OAuth app in the Zoom App Marketplace.
Give the app the scopes to create, update and delete meetings (meeting:write:admin, or the granular meeting scopes).
Activate the app, then copy its account id, client id and client secret.
Save them below in the Zoom form (they are stored encrypted and checked with Zoom first).
Turn on the hire.scheduling.zoom feature flag in Settings, Feature flags.
Organisers need a Zoom user in that account with their email, or set one host user for every interview.
